result_semantic_payload.summary: All USDT transfers visible in the seized device's logs are attributed to the account name "chenwei" in /logs/app1.log: (1) 2024-03-01 09:15:03, 30000 USDT to dest=TBait8888Wallet, bracketed by LOGIN user=chenwei ip=203.0.113.77 at 09:14:22 and LOGOUT at 09:16:44; (2) 2024-03-02 22:43:55, 12000 USDT to dest=TBait8888Wallet, bracketed by LOGIN user=chenwei ip=198.51.100.23 at 22:41:10. Total 42000 USDT, single destination wallet. No USDT transfers appear in /logs/app2.log (that log contains only LOGIN/UPLOAD/PRINT events for chenwei on 10.20.0.x addresses). The account name "chenwei" also appears in app2.log, but the README.txt scope note explicitly states the two internal systems "share no account database." Therefore same-named accounts across the two systems CANNOT be treated as the same person on the basis of this evidence: the name is the only shared attribute, there is no cross-system identifier (no SSO, AD, hash, email, hardware ID, or correlated timestamp), and the two systems show disjoint network ranges (10.20.0.5 / 10.20.0.9 vs 203.0.113.77 / 198.51.100.23). The evidence supports only: (a) a log-recorded actor named "chenwei" performed both transfers in app1.log; (b) a log-recorded actor named "chenwei" performed unrelated office activities in app2.log; (c) the two "chenwei" records cannot be merged into a single identified person from this device's logs alone. Attribution of the transfers to the human employee Chenwei (finance dept) is plausible but unproven — it requires external corroboration (HR identity, credential/AD records, wallet KYC for TBait8888Wallet). Note also that the delegated scope says 'windows', but the task context reports platforms=[] and no source_scopes; the available evidence is generic log files, not Windows-native artifacts (no registry, Event Log, Prefetch, Amcache), so the Windows-specialist corroboration rules (execution claims require Prefetch/Amcache) cannot be applied here.

claim_candidates.text: Both USDT transfers visible in the device logs are attributed to the account name 'chenwei' in /logs/app1.log: 30000 USDT on 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT on 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both to destination wallet TBait8888Wallet (total 42000 USDT).

The 2024-03-01 transfer was performed within a chenwei session from ip=203.0.113.77 (LOGIN 09:14:22, TRANSFER 09:15:03, LOGOUT 09:16:44); the 2024-03-02 transfer followed a chenwei LOGIN from ip=198.51.100.23 at 22:41:10.
No USDT or any TRANSFER event appears in /logs/app2.log; its only chenwei activities are LOGIN (10.20.0.5, 10.20.0.9), UPLOAD of /shared/annual-plan.docx, and a PRINT job to printer HQ-3F.

Same-named accounts across the two systems cannot be treated as the same person based on this evidence: the only shared attribute is the literal string 'chenwei', and the scope note states the two internal systems share no account database.
limitations: Absence of a shared account database is stated in the case-scope README, not independently verified from registry/AD artifacts.
No cross-system identifier (SSO ticket, account hash, email, hardware ID) exists in the evidence to bridge the two systems.

claim_candidates.text: The two systems show disjoint network ranges (app2.log: 10.20.0.5 and 10.20.0.9 private addresses; app1.log: 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 public/documentation-range addresses), which is consistent with two separate environments rather than one identity spanning both.

Attributing the transfers to the human employee Chenwei (finance dept, office workstation) is plausible but unproven; it requires external corroboration such as HR identity records, credential/AD logs, or wallet KYC for TBait8888Wallet.
limitations: Log 'user=' fields are self-reported by the application and can be spoofed or shared.
No authentication artifact (password hash, session token, device ID) is present in the evidence.
README.txt is a case-scope note, not an authenticated HR record.

claim_candidates.text: Destination wallet TBait8888Wallet receives both transfers, making it the single common financial endpoint across the two transfer events.
